I went from a 3060 to a 7800xt and I’ve finally been able to step up to 1440p. Even at 1080p, the 3060 was struggling with frame drops as low as 10-20fps at times. It was also consistently below 50 at 1440p and the 7800xt effectively doubled the performance in HD2. It didn’t hurt to get it on sale at 7700xt levels of pricing.

One reason the 7800 xt doesn't look great vs the 6800 xt is that the 6800, 6800 xt and 6900 xt were all Navi 21 while the 6700 xt and 6700 were Navi 22. Both the 7800 xt and 7700 xt are Navi 32 so the 7800 xt is actually the successor to the 6700 xt and the 7700 xt is to tbe 6700.

It might be bit of a stretch to say it’s a 5 year you given games like Black Myth, star wars, alan wake 2, avatar are already struggling without upscaling. 

The 6700 xt is only 3.5 years old, and it’s already well below 60fps at 1080p in plenty of games.

Now in 2025, this card is not getting very good performance in newer games without compromises being made to settings, especially with more games mandating ray tracing.

comments.text:
IF you have high refresh rate 1440p and 4K monitors - you can ignore this ramble - it ain't meant for you 😀

Right - so 1080p...
I mean - Looking at it from a mid range sorta view - the biggest issues for these two cards is ACTUALLY a totally different place than most are looking. Think about it. You have the 6650 XT at 235$ and 7600 at 230$ which falls behind the 7700 XT by "only" about 20-25% - but that card is near as makes no difference 2x the price with its 450$. Then we have the next issue - the 6700 (Non XT) at 270$ where that advantage shrinks to about 10-15% - at 180$ less....

Now - this is where it SERIOUSLY begins to hurt! The RX 6750 XT at 360$ - This is still 90$ less - which at this price point - is around a full tier difference. Like the 7700 XT - this is a 12GB card - but surely the new card does better here - right? Well sure if you load up the right games and tests - the 7700 XT wins......... however in others it gets ABSOLUTELY CURBSTOMPED! An example of this is Doom Eternal. Here the 7700 XT has an average at around 170-ish FPS in 1440p ... The 6750 XT 220-ish FPS. That's a pretty large difference... 
But never mind that - even when it comes to the games where the 6750 XT falls behind - it's by 1-10% at worst... That's not great at 20% less than the 450$ mark.

Now ignoring the 6800 XT which in my mind is WAY overpriced right now at the same price as the 7800 XT even if they are fairly evenly matched - due to the AV1 and other more modern feature sets ... But what about the 6900 XT? It's 580$... so 80$ more however that shouldn't be that close - AND the 6950 XT is just 50$ more than that at 630$...

I'm not suggesting that you shouldn't buy the 7800 XT - that's not my point here. My point is that AMD is its own worst enemy. Frankly the 7800 XT is priced "perfectly" - the 7700 XT not so much really... at 399$ it would be much more attractive - at 450 - you just seem plain dumb if you don't spend the last 50$ and get the 7800 XT instead... The "perfect" price of the 7800 XT is the issue though. There is no uplift in performance for your money. To the 90%+ of gamers who still play on 1080p monitors - you will have EXACTLY the same game experience if you pick up an RX 7600/RX 6650 XT - as you will from a 7800 XT. I can attest to this since we have one of these cards and have tested Starfield on it. 1080p maxed except for one of the settings which gives a lot of systems issues - so I just reduced it right away without testing with it because I can't tell the difference (Called something like "colliding shadows" or something like that - has been set to low) It ran butter smooth. Like actually I couldn't tell the difference between it an my main rig when using the same monitor. The problem here is we are talking a 235$ card vs a 500$ card. The "smaller" 7600/6650 XT are just too good at that price... It's not that the 7800 XT isn't better - because it is! probably by 50% if you run the right tests! But let's just take the 7600. If that card is 230$, has the same feature sets like AV1 as the 7700 XT and the 7800 XT, AND the on top of this performs like a champ at 1080p gaming, then we have to have a serious debate about what you are getting for you 220 and 270$ more respectively. The V-RAM - sure - but that can quickly be mitigated by removing a few of the "high intensity" setting down a single nudge - which you most likely won't be able to tell at 1080p anyway. Now we have the FPS - well if the FPS is already in the 60+ (some WAY more depending on the game) on the 7600 - then how much more are you getting from the 7700 XT? It's it worth 2x the price? I think it wont be to most people if they knew what they were buying instead of listening to bad advice.

500 USD today is equivalent to about 425 USD in 2020, when the 6800 XT first launched at 650 USD, which is equivalent to about 770 USD today, which is about what you can buy the 6800 XT's true successor for (the 7900 XT).

The 7800 XT is not a 6800 XT successor, it's a 6700 XT successor. The naming is dumb, but you have to consider that inflation has been a lot higher than normal over the past three years, and AMD can only take a small portion of the blame for that, unless Lisa Su is secretely running the global economy XD

The 7800 XT is using a mid-sized GPU, and it's launching at a similar MSRP to what the 6700 XT launched at. 500 USD today is equivalent to around 440 USD two and a half years ago, when the 6700 XT first launched at 480 USD, and the 7800 XT is about 43% faster than the 6700 XT.

It's nothing new for previous gen graphics cards to be heavily discounted in price before many of the next gen cards replace them, and for them to have equal or better performance per dollar at those prices, yet many people are arguing things like "the 7800 XT offers little to no improvement in value per dollar over the previous generation", as if AMD is supposed to give us a major improvement in value per dollar over CURRENT pricing for the already heavily discounted 6800 XT (and other various heavily discounted 6000 series cards). 

Do you need to like the price of the 7800 XT? No. It sucks that average incomes haven't kept pace with inflation, and you could argue that AMD does share some degree of blame for that, though certainly not most of the blame. 

The 4070 is also somewhat underrated because people are failing to account for the higher than normal inflation that we've had over the past three years, and despite it having less Vram, which definitely is a disadvantage, DLSS is better than FSR, and the 4070 does have significantly better power efficiency, which is always going to come with a price premium, whether you like it or not, especially when the box says Nvidia on it. The 6700 XT is currently a potentially very good option at 330 USD, but stock will probably mostly run out long before the next generation comes out, and the 7700 XT is simply too close in manufacturing cost to the 7800 XT for AMD to ever want to give us a genuinely good deal on them for an extended period of time. AMD definitely left a big gap between the 7600 (which is itself still over-priced at most retailers), and the 7800 XT, basically forcing people to buy previous gen, or used cards, if they want a good value lower-mid-range or upper-low-end graphics card, and Nvidia has also basically done the same thing, by offering poor value for everything below the RTX 4070.
